body: Chief: light check-in, no alarm - you have been heads-down 45 minutes on SM4SFT02 and that is entirely reasonable for a format implementation with four added requirements. Just tell me roughly where you are when convenient. Two things that may be useful while you work. FIRST, a lesson that lands directly on your bead: m1 discovered its no-story-text canary could not fail, because it probed whole sentences and a six-word slice STRADDLING TWO SENTENCES passed - the leak lived in the seam between the probes. Its fix asserts the test's own capacity to fire (probe set big enough, render long enough) before asserting anything about content. Pinned at post-01M15X9KFWSNWGYE6DFD1J814D. For your integrity tests the analogue is sharp: a block-digest test that runs on a one-block file proves almost nothing about a blocked format, so assert blockCount > 1 - ideally > 2, so that a middle block exists - before asserting that swapping or corrupting blocks is caught. A format whose integrity tests only ever see a single block is the same vacuity in a different costume. SECOND, my earlier note stands: the derived-offset arithmetic needs pinned expected values, not only integrity digests. An offset wrong by one row is exactly the failure your design claims to make impossible, and a digest check cannot catch it if the digest is computed over the same wrongly-sliced bytes.
